limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: bash

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

"""Reproduce the malformed header and verify the normal header."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0,str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))
import pytest
from parser import MalformedHeaderError, parse_header
def test_missing_colon_raises(malformed_header):
    with pytest.raises(MalformedHeaderError, match="missing ':' separator"):
        parse_header(malformed_header)
def test_wellformed_header_ok():
    assert parse_header('Content-Length: 42') == ('Content-Length','42')

{"command":"cd /testbed && python - <<'EOF'
import json, re, subprocess
import pytest
from parser import parse_header, MalformedHeaderError

# 1) Run the reproduction suite and capture per-test outcomes
proc = subprocess.run(
    ["python", "-m", "pytest", "incoming/repro_tests", "-v", "--tb=short"],
    capture_output=True, text=True,
)
tests = {}
for m in re.finditer(r"^incoming/repro_tests/\S+::(\w+)\s+(PASSED|FAILED|ERROR)", proc.stdout, re.M):
    tests[m.group(1)] = "passed" if m.group(2) == "PASSED" else "failed"
passed = proc.returncode == 0 and len(tests) == 2

# 2) Verify the expected malformed-header exception using the same input
#    the fixture produces (collection-time shell helper output, stripped).
malformed = open("incoming/repro_tests/malformed_header.txt").read().strip()
try:
    parse_header(malformed)
    exception = {"type": None, "message": None}
except MalformedHeaderError as e:
    exception = {"type": type(e).__name__, "message": str(e)}

# 3) Also verify the well-formed behavior (reported for completeness below)
wellformed = parse_header("Content-Length: 42")

report = {
    "exception": exception,
    "tests": tests,
    "passed": passed,
}
with open("artifacts/parser_repro.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(report, f, indent=2)
    f.write("\n")

print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
print("wellformed ->", wellformed, sep="\n")
EOF"}
